Real advance command by an implementor: 'Initiating autowiz.' at CMP / LVL_IMMORT / file FALSE after the rise message and before the (absent) child process, once per level gained at or above LVL_IMMORT, with the level and brief-syslog filters. Nothing is spawned: the reference oracle has no autowiz binary. Control autowiz-producer. Oracle vehicle: advance a peer to 31 watched by a complete-syslog immortal; the corpus scenario set does not stage it, so this is unit-green.

Real Lua log() through the engine's bridge: the success arm writes the file at BRF / LVL_IMMORT / TRUE, the bad-argument arm logs its own line at BRF / LVL_IMMORT / FALSE and returns 1, and a number argument coerces (lua_isstring) into the success arm. Control lua-log-file-flag. No shipped non-archive script calls log(), so unit-green only.

DP-1404. C's failed-fopen arm: a character entering with no crash file, which is every new character's first entry. Oracle mudlog-crash-load-entry drives a save, then reallyquit outside a save room (LOSTEQ), then the menu's 1: extraction deleted the RENT_CRASH file (persist.crash-file-removed-at-extraction), so the next entry is this arm, seen by an in-game God at NRM / MAX(LVL_IMMORT, invis) / file TRUE. Also proved through the real creation flow (TestCrashLoadFirstEntryProducer), which pins it immediately before do_start's advance_level producer. A below-immortal, brief-syslog and writing observer see nothing, and entering alone never creates an object save. Controls no-equipment and producer-off.

DP-1404. RENT_RENTED: object_saves.kind 2, written by the legal quit and the idle force-rent, so this is every ordinary re-login after a lawful exit. Oracle mudlog-crash-load-entry (second arm: quit in the temple, then the menu's 1) has an in-game God receive '%s un-renting and entering game.' at NRM / MAX(LVL_IMMORT, invis) / file TRUE; the rent file survives extraction, so the code is still there. Control unrenting.

DP-1404. RENT_CRASH: object_saves.kind 1, written by save, autosave, shutdown/reboot and the idle void pull. '%s retrieving crash-saved items and entering game.' at NRM / MAX(LVL_IMMORT, invis) / file TRUE; the same entry then rewrites the header to RENT_CRASH (:659-663). Unit-green only, deliberately: a retained RENT_CRASH file needs an unclean or unextracted stop, and the harness's <CRASH> and <RESTART> vehicles both forbid passive peers, so no in-game immortal can witness the relogin. Every route to this arm that an immortal could watch is closed by the file's lifetime - a legal quit rewrites the header to RENT_RENTED, and a LOSTEQ quit makes extraction delete it (persist.crash-file-removed-at-extraction). Control crash-saved.
